summary: Add Number.isFinite() validation alongside existing typeof checks in the /calculate, /memory/add, and /memory/subtract request handlers so that non-finite numeric inputs (Infinity, -Infinity, NaN) are rejected with a 400 error instead of silently producing a null result in a 200 response.
goal: Requests containing non-finite numeric values (e.g. 1e400 parsed as Infinity) are rejected at the HTTP request-validation layer with the existing 400 'Invalid request' error shape, matching the already-documented 400 response path in the OpenAPI spec.
background: JSON.parse('{"a":1e400}') yields a === Infinity because 1e400 is a valid JSON number literal whose magnitude collapses to Infinity per the ECMAScript Number grammar. typeof Infinity === "number", so the existing typeof check accepts it. The handler then computes a non-finite result and JSON.stringify silently turns Infinity into null in the HTTP 200 response body instead of routing to the existing 400 'Invalid request' path. This is a correctness gap in the existing input-validation layer.

in_scope.text: Add Number.isFinite() guard alongside each existing typeof !== "number" check in the /calculate handler in src/server.ts
Add Number.isFinite() guard alongside each existing typeof !== "number" check in the /memory/add handler in src/server.ts
Add Number.isFinite() guard alongside each existing typeof !== "number" check in the /memory/subtract handler in src/server.ts
Reuse the existing 400 error-response shapes: { "error": "invalid request: require op, a, b" } and { "error": "invalid request: require value" } — no new error shape

out_of_scope.text: Changes to openapi/openapi.yaml or contracts/*.ocl — the existing 400 response path is already documented
New automated tests — this is a thin/L1 profile fix; the existing test suite establishes no regression
New endpoints, new response fields, or any other product feature additions
Handling of NaN produced internally (as opposed to NaN supplied in the request body)

assumptions: Only src/server.ts is touched; no contract, OpenAPI, or OCL files require modification
The existing 400 error-response shapes are sufficient to communicate the rejection of non-finite input
The three handlers identified (calculate, memory/add, memory/subtract) are the only HTTP request handlers that parse numeric input from the request body
constraints: Do not introduce new error shapes or new response fields
Do not modify openapi/openapi.yaml or any contracts/*.ocl file
The fix must not break the existing test suite (3 test files, 21 tests)

success_criteria.text: POST /calculate with a non-finite numeric operand (e.g. {op:add,a:1e400,b:1}) returns HTTP 400 with {"error":"invalid request: require op, a, b"}
POST /memory/add with a non-finite numeric value (e.g. {value:1e400}) returns HTTP 400 with {"error":"invalid request: require value"}
POST /memory/subtract with a non-finite numeric value (e.g. {value:1e400}) returns HTTP 400 with {"error":"invalid request: require value"}
Normal finite-input requests (e.g. POST /calculate {op:add,a:2,b:3}) continue to return HTTP 200 with the correct result
All 21 pre-existing automated tests continue to pass

human_gate.reason: Fix is a small, well-understood validation addition confined to the HTTP request layer. No contract surface, no new error shape, no ambiguity.
